To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Mn2+ is required for activation of threonine-dehydrogenase, that the activation process is thiol-dependent, that stoichiometry of Mn-binding is 0.86:1 (mol:Mn/mol subunit), that Kd = 8.6 microM, and that Mn2+ interacts directly with the enzyme.
L-threonine is dehydrogenated to alpha-ketobutyrate by a thiol-dependent enzyme that is activated by Mn2+.
Mn2+ is a required cofactor for L-threonine DH activity and that the enzyme has a single Mn2+-binding site with a Kd = 8.6 microM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of the L-threonine catabolic enzymes from Escherichiacoli K-12.
the purification, characterization, and kinetic analysis of the enzyme, L-threoninase, from the bacterium Escherichia coil.
the purification and characterization of L-threonine (L-threo) dehydrogenase, a pyridine nucleotide-dependent enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of L-threo to alpha-ketobutyrate.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Mn2+ activation of the enzyme is not due to a metal ion cofactor effect.
